custom_logic_notes: Self-learning EA using virtual order simulation. For each detected binary pattern (up to 2^(NN-1) types), across multiple delta parameters (Nidelt=20) and SL/TP levels (Nstop=1), it opens virtual orders and tracks whether price hits virtual TP or SL first. Results are stored as probability weights (Store_PowerUp/PowerDn) with exponential forgetting (forg=1.05). Real trades open only when: (1) probability exceeds Probab threshold, (2) virtual trade count exceeds 10, (3) at least 2*Period bars since last trade. Pattern detection: on each tick, if price moves beyond PatternDeltaParameter from last pattern point, a new point is pushed into the sliding window. The pattern is encoded as a binary number (1=price up from previous, 0=down). Close signals also generated when opposite-direction probability increases by >0.05 or when probability >0.6 with position in profit. Learning history can be saved/loaded from files for persistence across sessions.
python_conversion_notes: The core challenge is replicating the virtual order simulation and probability accumulation system. The self-learning mechanism must maintain state across bars: for each pattern combination, delta parameter, and stop level, track virtual order open prices and update PowerUp/PowerDn weights on virtual TP/SL hits. The forgetting factor (forg) means recent outcomes weighted more heavily. Binary pattern encoding is straightforward to replicate. File persistence for learning history needs replacement (pickle/CSV). The EA runs on every tick with pattern shift detection, so tick data is essential for accurate backtesting. TimeToUpdate gate (2*Period*60 seconds) limits real trade frequency. Close signal logic has two paths: probability delta >0.05 and probability >0.6 with profit threshold - both must be implemented. No standard indicators are used; the entire signal system is custom adaptive logic.
